fact_sheet.business_description: Prudential plc is a UK-headquartered group comprising Asian insurance/asset management operations and Jackson National, a US-based annuity provider [D01]. The group structure faces questions regarding the optimality of separating the distinct regulatory and market-sensitive businesses [D01].
segments_and_separable_assets: Asia: H1 2019 external revenue £16,105m, operating profit £1,198m [D06]
US (Jackson National): H1 2019 external revenue £24,465m, operating profit £1,215m [D06]
Eastspring: Asset management arm with £169.5bn AUM [D03]
economics_vs_peers: Asia segment reported 14% constant currency profit growth; US segment reported 14% constant currency profit growth in H1 2019 [D06]
Jackson RBC ratio >400%; Solvency II coverage 222% [D03]
US peers (MetLife, AIG, Lincoln National) trade at 0.60x–0.74x P/B, providing comparison for Jackson's capital-intensive nature [D04]
capital_structure: Group Solvency II surplus estimated at £16.7bn [D02]
event_or_catalyst_evidence: Third Point sent a letter on 2020-02-24 advocating for the separation of the US (Jackson) and Asian businesses [D01]
Management previously announced preparation for a European demerger (M&G) [D03]
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Volatility of US annuity guarantees and sensitivity to equity/rate correlation [D05]
Potential costs of disentanglement and requirement for fresh capital in a separation [D05]
Asia-specific risks including currency, regulation, and distribution [D05]
recent_events: 2020-02-24: Third Point public letter sent to Prudential plc [D01]
third_point_context: Third Point is actively engaging via a public letter as of 2020-02-24 [D01]

event_identified.evidence: Third Point is advocating for the separation of Prudential's US and Asian businesses to unlock value from the conglomerate structure [D01].

edge.evidence: Third Point identifies a clear conglomerate discount and provides the strategic rationale for separating distinct, capital-intensive businesses to improve market valuation [D01].

governance_route_or_process.evidence: The firm is engaging publicly with a specific plan for separation, following the company's recent precedent of demerging M&G [D01, D03].

downside_floor.evidence: The group maintains strong solvency with a £16.7bn Solvency II surplus and Jackson's RBC ratio above 400% [D02, D03].

size_and_liquidity.evidence: With a market cap of £33.79bn, Prudential provides sufficient liquidity for Third Point to build a meaningful position [D04].

management_credibility.evidence: Management has previously demonstrated an ability to execute major corporate separations via the M&G demerger [D03].

gate1.edge_statement: Third Point will drive the separation of Prudential's US annuity business and high-growth Asian insurance operations to eliminate the conglomerate discount and align capital structures with peer benchmarks.
gate1.one_line_verdict: a conglomerate with distinct regulatory and growth profiles that can be unlocked via separation, mirroring the company's own prior demerger process.

gate2.variant_view: The market currently conflates Prudential's high-growth Asian insurance business with the capital-intensive US annuity business (Jackson), resulting in an inefficient conglomerate structure that trades at a discount to the sum of its parts. We believe separating these entities will allow the Asian operations to be valued as a pure-play growth insurer while enabling Jackson to optimize its capital structure independently. This separation will eliminate the persistent conglomerate discount and unlock significant shareholder value, mirroring the success of the M&G demerger [D01].
evidence: Prudential comprises two distinct, capital-intensive businesses with different regulatory and market profiles, hindering valuation [D01].
The company successfully executed a prior demerger of M&G, proving the operational feasibility of such a split [D03].
US peers like MetLife and AIG trade at lower P/B multiples (0.60x–0.74x), highlighting the drag of the US annuity business on the group's current 2.31x P/B valuation [D04].
gate2.peer_benchmark: US peers (MetLife, AIG, Lincoln National) trade at 0.60x–0.74x P/B [D04]
what_must_be_true: Regulatory approval for the separation of US and Asian operations can be secured without prohibitive capital requirements.
The Asian business can sustain its growth trajectory as an independent entity.
Jackson can operate efficiently as a standalone entity with its existing >400% RBC ratio.
Management remains committed to value-unlocking corporate simplification.

arithmetic: Asia segment value at 15x P/E (peer multiple) on £2.4bn annualized H1 profit: £36bn [D06]
Jackson segment value at 0.7x P/B (peer benchmark) on adjusted book value: £18bn [D04]

floor.basis: Solvency II surplus of £16.7bn plus regulatory capital redundancy in Jackson [D02, D03]

flagged_assumptions: Annualized H1 2019 profit for Asia used as proxy for full-year run rate
Adjustment of book value for Jackson segment based on reported peer multiples
No significant capital leakage during separation

gate4.escalation_path: If management remains unresponsive to the private/public case, we will consider escalating via board nominations or increased public pressure ahead of the next AGM cycle.
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: In our current mega-cap constructivist era, we prioritize private engagement but utilize public letters when the strategic path is clear—as it is here given the recent M&G split—and management requires public pressure to accelerate corporate simplification.

kill_criteria: Management formally rejects the separation proposal and closes the strategic review process [D01].
Regulatory authorities impose prohibitive capital charges on a standalone Jackson entity [D05].
A significant market downturn leads to a sharp decline in Jackson's RBC ratio below required thresholds [D05].
The Asia business experiences a multi-quarter growth deceleration failing to justify a premium valuation [D05].
gate5.portfolio_risk: We maintain exposure to financials and mega-cap conglomerates; this position adds to our UK/European-listed insurance and insurance-adjacent holdings, increasing exposure to interest rate and equity market volatility [D01, D05].
gate5.hedge_overlay: Index puts and selective shorts in US annuity-exposed financial peers to mitigate tail risk from Jackson's sensitivity to equity/rate correlation [D05].
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The primary risk is that the complex regulatory and capital disentanglement of Jackson National from the Asian operations proves more costly and capital-intensive than currently modeled, eroding the expected SOTP value.

final.what_would_change_our_mind: A formal and permanent rejection of the separation strategy by the board, or a material regulatory shift that makes the separation of Jackson capital-prohibitive, destroying the SOTP upside.
final.memo:
Prudential plc is a premier insurance group saddled with a structural conglomerate discount that obscures the true value of its high-growth Asian operations [D01]. The market currently misprices the company by aggregating a capital-intensive US annuity business, Jackson National, with a high-growth Asian insurance franchise, resulting in a valuation that fails to reflect the intrinsic worth of the underlying segments [D01, D06].

Our sum-of-the-parts analysis, based on a 15x P/E multiple for the Asia segment and a 0.7x P/B benchmark for Jackson, yields an implied equity value of £46.3bn [D04, D06]. Against a current market capitalization of £33.8bn, this implies significant upside potential to our target of 1720p per share [D04, D06].

The market’s persistent discount is a direct function of the current inefficient structure, which forces investors to hold a hybrid risk profile of Asian growth and US annuity volatility [D01, D05]. A separation will resolve this misalignment, allowing investors to value the Asian business as a pure-play growth insurer, similar to its high-growth peers [D01].

We are calling for the full separation of the US annuity business, a path previously validated by the company's successful M&G demerger [D01, D03]. We expect Mike Wells and Paul Manduca to accelerate this process over the next four quarters [D01]. We stand ready to escalate our engagement if management ignores this clear path to shareholder value [D01].

The downside is protected by a robust balance sheet, including a £16.7bn Solvency II surplus and Jackson’s RBC ratio exceeding 400% [D02, D03]. We will exit the position immediately if management abandons the strategy or if regulatory hurdles render the split value-destructive [D01, D05].

We are initiating a 5% position in the common equity [D05]. We are sizing this for high conviction, with a targeted 25% IRR, while hedging our exposure to US annuity-related market risks through selective index puts and financial sector shorts [D05].
